text:
kevin: heads-up: during a recruiter dry-run yesterday we discovered that the "scorecard_type" field was mapped to the wrong role. engineering candidates are getting the "product_manager" rubric in the interview UI.

nina: wow. how widespread? was this from the bulk-import we ran last night?

kevin: yes, looks like the nightly CSV import mapped `role_slug`->`scorecard_type` using a fallback map that had stale entries. I sampled 10 recent interviews and 7/10 had the wrong rubric.

sam: tagging ATS infra: did the import job change? i thought we added a new fallback for legacy role names.

ats-bot: webhook: bulk-import job #import-2025-11-30 completed. Rows=642. Source=legacy-hiring-exports.

kevin: impact: 7 interviews with wrong rubrics; 3 are live this AM. risk: incorrect candidate scoring and potential biased banding in debriefs.

jess: Recruiting ops: can you pause interview debrief submissions for the affected panels until we confirm correct rubrics? we should avoid locking in scores under wrong rubric.

nina: i can message the schedulers and request a hold on debrief submission. also will post an all-interviewer note in the calibration channel.

sam: mitigation plan: 1) revert import mapping to previous stable map 2) re-run a targeted import for the affected rows with corrected mapping 3) attach an "alert: scorecard-mismatch" banner to the UI for affected interviews so interviewers know to ignore previous rubric fields when submitting.

kevin: can we automate detection for this in future? e.g., when the ATS sends an interview create event compare `role_slug` -> served `scorecard_type` and raise an anomaly if mismatch.

sam: yes. i'll add a lightweight webhook validator that runs before publish. if mismatch probability > 0 we mark the import row as failed and notify the ops channel.

people-ops-bot: ticket created: RECRUIT-1983 "bulk-import mapping produced wrong scorecard assignment". Assignees=sam,nina.

jess: follow-ups: 1) people-ops to notify affected hiring managers + provide template communication; 2) engineering to add import sanity checks and a dry-run validation step; 3) recruiting to run manual audit of any interviews from the last 48h.

nina: i'll handle the comms and audit. starting now. posting affected candidate IDs to the secure channel.

kevin: thanks all. once remedied we should retroactively flag any debriefs submitted under the wrong rubric and prompt re-eval. also adding to interviewer-playbook: "if rubric looks off, pause debrief and message people-ops".

sam: created quick PR to add mapping validation + UI banner toggle. will roll to staging for a smoke test.

kevin: staging smoke looks good. planning to re-run corrected import at 05:30 UTC, then clear UI banner.

jess: appreciated. this could have been worse — nice catch during the dry-run. will follow up with a short training note for schedulers about verifying role->rubric mapping when using legacy exports. :white_check_mark:
